Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
715 PM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 219 PM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 219 PM EDT Sunday...

1. A weak, moisture starved, cold front will pass through the 
area tomorrow, with sharply colder temperatures heading towards 
mid week.

2. Moderating temperatures are expected late this week and next 
weekend with some brief rain possible Thursday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 219 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure today will begin to depart tonight into 
tomorrow evening with the approach of a weak, moisture starved cold 
front for tomorrow. GOES-19 visible satellite shows this front 
nicely with a narrow band of cloud cover stretched across the 
Michigan Upper Peninsula to west central Quebec. As the front moves 
into northern New York tomorrow morning, antecedent dry conditions 
at the surface will limit much if not all of the precipitation that 
will be associated with the boundary. Virga looks likely with 
dewpoint depressions of 5-10 degrees ahead of the front. A few 
places along the northwest facing slopes of the Adirondacks and 
northern Greens, including Jay Peak, may see a few sprinkles, but 
accumulations will be little to non-measureable. In the deeper 
valleys, we will likely not have enough time to saturate before dry 
air advects in behind the boundary cutting off any precipitation 
chances by tomorrow early afternoon. Winds will turn to the north-
northwest as the front moves through advecting sharply colder air 
from Canada. Monday night lows will cool to the upper 20s for many 
locations with a few locations hovering around the freezing mark in 
the wider valleys. Tuesday will feature sunny skies with continued 
cool high temperatures struggling to reach the upper 40s. The 
coldest night of the season arrives Tuesday night under strong 
radiational cooling. Overnight lows may approach some records for 
Montpelier and St. Johnsbury, with records elsewhere residing in the 
10th percentile or lower. Temperatures will drop to the teens across 
the Adirondacks and low 20s elsewhere. Temperatures slowly rebound 
Wednesday as high pressure and south winds help to moderate our flow 
pattern.

KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure overhead will allow the air mass to slowly 
moderate Wednesday night into next weekend with highs climbing back 
into the upper 50s and 60s on Thursday and Friday. There is the 
potential for a few showers on Thursday night with another weak cold 
front, about 30-60% chance of rain outside of central and south-
central Vermont, which have lower chances, closer to 10-40%. The 
forecast for Halloween trick-or-treating looks dry and seasonably 
mild under high pressure with afternoon temperatures in the upper 
50s to mid 60s, falling into the lower and mid 50s in the evening.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 00Z Tuesday...VFR conditions and light winds are expected to
prevail through at least 12Z-17Z Monday as cloud coverage 
gradually increases overnight and ceilings lower aft 12z. Ceilings 
could wobble around the VFR-MVFR threshold towards 15Z-18Z 
Monday with the frontal passage,

Light SSW winds overnight then swithcing NW with cold Fropa Mon
aftn. 

A Monday morning rain shower is possible at MSS ahead of 
and along the front from 13Z-17Z, but otherwise dry conditions 
are anticipated at the TAF sites over the next 24 hours.
